title: Unified Inference - Product overview, PRD, design specs, roadmap, pricing, and Q3 2028 release notes
author: Ava Martinez
summary: This hub document consolidates the current product overview, PRD-level requirements, high-level design specs, roadmap themes for the next 6 quarters, pricing and packaging guidance, and the Q3 2028 release notes and rollout plan for Unified Inference.
body:
Overview:

Unified Inference is Redwood Inference's unified product surface that provides a consistent API and operational experience across Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private deployments. This document consolidates the PRD, key requirements, design constraints, roadmap themes, pricing and packaging guidance, and the Q3 2028 release notes and rollout plan.

Goals and success metrics:
- Make it trivial for engineering teams to migrate from hosted to dedicated/private deployments without code changes.
- Reduce per-token cost for typical RLHF-style chat workloads by 25% through batching, KV caching, and model variant routing by end of 2028.
- Maintain 99.95% availability for production customers on Dedicated plans under committed capacity.
- Provide first-class rollout tooling (canary/A-B/fallback) and per-route observability in Redwood Console.

1) PRD & Requirements (high level):

Audience: product, engineering, platform, and customer success.

Key functional requirements:
1.0 Core API parity
  1.1 Text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking endpoints must have identical request/response shapes across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
  1.2 Streaming and function/tool-calling primitives must be supported end-to-end.

2.0 Deployment portability
  2.1 Customers must be able to pin model versions and rollout policies independent of infrastructure.
  2.2 A migration path (CLI + infra templates) from Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private with minimal config changes (<= 3 fields).

3.0 Performance & economics
  3.1 Median p95 latency for small-chat workloads (<= 256 tokens) should be <= 120ms on Dedicated pools under target utilization.
  3.2 Default model routing rules should reduce expected per-token cost by >= 15% via cheaper model variants and quantized kernels for compatible requests.

4.0 Reliability & fallbacks
  4.1 Automatic fallback to compatible model variants or region replication when capacity is constrained.
  4.2 Canary and auto-rollbacks for model rollouts with configurable error rate thresholds.

Non-functional constraints:
- Security: Must integrate with KMS/HSM for customer-managed keys in Private deployments.
- Compliance: Support audit logging for all inference requests (customer-visible ID + token usage) for enterprise customers.

2) Design specs (high level):

Architecture overview:
- Serving runtime: GPU-optimized engine that supports continuous batching, KV cache management, and quantization-aware execution paths.
- Smart routing: Policy engine to route by latency, cost, region, or customer tier, with deterministic fallback chains.
- Control plane: Deployment abstraction layer that stores model manifests, rollout policies, and per-customer overrides.

API & schema notes (examples):
- Generation endpoint (POST /v1/generation): request fields: model, input, max_tokens, temperature, stream (bool), route_policy_id
- Rollout policy manifest (YAML): name, target_model_versions[], canary_percentage, rollback_on_error_rate

Key design decisions and trade-offs:
- Use single request/response shape to simplify SDKs and customers' implementation effort. This increases transformation work in the control plane but reduces surface area for SDKs.
- Prioritize latency for small-chat workloads; aggressive batching for high-throughput batch jobs will be scheduled on separate pools.

Minimal API compatibility table (text):
Feature | Hosted | Dedicated | Private
Streaming | Yes | Yes | Yes
Function calling | Yes | Yes | Yes
Model pinning | Yes | Yes | Yes
KMS integration | Managed | Optional | Required (customer)

3) Roadmap & themes (Q3 2028 planning horizon):

North star themes for next 6 quarters:
- Q3-Q4 2028: "Production economics" - cost controls (batching, cache hints), model quantization profiles, per-route cost analytics.
- Q1 2029: "Enterprise readiness" - expanded compliance packages, longer retention for observability, SLA tiers for Dedicated.
- Q2 2029: "Private-first" - simplified on-prem installer, air-gapped deployment guides, automated onprem upgrades.

Quarterly milestones (high level):
- 2028 Q3: Launch v3 rollout engine (canary + auto-rollback), publish pricing tiers for Dedicated, release KV-cache improvements that reduce cold-start token cost by ~12%.
- 2028 Q4: Add quantization profiles for two canonical model families and Console support for per-model cost projections.
- 2029 Q1: Private deployment GA (with KMS integration and enterprise packaging).

Stakeholders and signals to watch:
- Observability: token-level cost/latency breakdown dashboards (ownership: eng-platform).
- Sales/CS: migration win rate and time-to-first-successful-Dedicated-deploy.
- Reliability: SLO burn rate and error budget consumption during rollout windows.

4) Pricing & packaging notes (guidance):

Goals: provide clear upgrade path from self-serve hosted to reserved Dedicated while protecting gross margin.

Pricing tiers (summary):
Tier | Billing model | Key limits | Typical customer
Self-Serve Hosted | usage (per-token / per-embedding) | rate limits, soft quotas | early-stage startups, experiments
Dedicated Standard | monthly commit (GPU pool hours) + usage | committed quota, burst cap | mid-market product teams
Dedicated Enterprise | annual contract + support | SLA, dedicated pool, longer retention | regulated & large customers
Private | platform license + optional infra | support windows, onprem packaging | financial & healthcare customers

Packaging notes:
- Offer 30/60/90 day migration credits to encourage migration from Hosted to Dedicated.
- Provide SKU for "Observability Retention Add-on" (90/365 day options).
- Model variant pricing: apply differential pricing for high-cost foundation models vs. quantized or distilled variants.

Billing & metering details (key fields):
- Metering granularity: per-token for generation / chat; per-vector for embeddings (rounded to 8-byte vectors).
- Discounting: multi-quarter committed capacity discounts negotiated during contract stage.

5) Q3 2028 Release notes (v3.4.0 - Unified Inference):

Release highlights:
- v3 rollout engine: Canary + auto rollback on error-rate thresholds, per-route canary percentages, and pre-check health gating.
- Backend KV-cache improvements that reduce latency variance for chat workloads and cut cold-start token cost ~12%.
- Initial quantization profiles (beta) for two model families (RefModelA, RefModelB) with Console toggles.
- Dedicated pricing tiers and migration credits made available in the Console billing portal.

Breaking changes & migration notes:
- Rollout manifest schema adds an optional "rollback_on_error_rate" field (default: 0.05). Customers using a strict earlier manifest will need to add the field or rely on default behavior.
- Minor API compatibility: new route_policy_id in generation requests is optional; older SDKs will continue to work but won't get routing benefits. Encourage updating SDKs to v2.1+.

Rollout plan (detailed):
1. Internal dogfood (2 weeks) - activate v3 rollout engine for non-customer infra and run simulated canaries on low-traffic routes.
2. Early access (4 weeks) - invite 5 Tier-1 customers to opt into canary rollouts; collect stability and telemetry.
3. Gradual public rollout (6 weeks) - enable default rollout engine for 50% of eligible customers with automatic monitoring and auto-rollback enabled.
4. GA (target) - all eligible customers with release notes and migration assistance.

Operational & support notes:
- Runbook: See runbook: /eng-sre/runbooks/unified-inference-rollout-2028.
- Escalation: Pager for high-severity rollout regressions -> eng-sre oncall -> runtime team.
- Monitoring: dashboards: "UnifiedInference: rollout-health", "TokenCost: per-model" (ownership: eng-platform).

Appendices:
A. Acceptance criteria (short): see acceptance_criteria field.
B. Requirements matrix (short): see requirements_table field.
C. Owners and contacts: see owners field.

Document history and decisions:
- 2028-07-15: PRD authored and approved by product.
- 2028-08-05: Design review with runtime and platform teams.
- 2028-09-01: Release notes updated after early access telemetry and GA date confirmed.

Per-token cost reduction >= 15% for default routing rules in representative workloads
Rollout engine canary + auto-rollback exercised successfully in 3 independent dogfood campaigns
